On 2022-10-13, the user wanted to manage websites for recursive crawling: start from one URL and continue indefinitely, avoid crawling a website twice, allow adding websites on demand, and let multiple crawlers work in parallel without conflicting.

On 2022-10-13, the assistant proposed adding a `crawl_queue` collection with `_id` (ObjectId), `website_id` (ObjectId referencing either `websites._id` or `classic_websites._id`), `website_type` (`immersive` or `classic`), `crawl_status` (such as `pending`, `crawling`, or `crawled`), optional `assigned_crawler_id` (string), and `timestamp` (Date when the site was added).

The assistant advised adding a seed website to `crawl_queue` as `pending`; each crawler should claim a pending, unassigned entry by setting its `assigned_crawler_id` and status to `crawling`, then mark it `crawled` when finished. Discovered links should be added to the relevant `websites` or `classic_websites` collection and queued as pending. The assistant said on-demand additions could likewise be inserted as pending queue entries.

On 2022-10-13, the user requested a synthesis of the final MongoDB schema and documentation for an immersive-website index and web crawler, then asked the assistant to continue when the response was split across messages.
The proposed MongoDB schema has seven collections: `websites`, `classic_websites`, `game_engines`, `platforms`, `web_crawls`, `crawl_errors`, and `crawl_queue`.

The proposed `websites` collection stores an ObjectId, URL, title, description, keyword strings, graphics object (polygon count and texture size), world object (size and environment), immersion type (VR, AR, or both), references to a game engine and platform, related immersive website IDs, classic referrer website IDs, and a crawl ID.

The proposed `classic_websites` collection stores an ObjectId, URL, title, description, keyword strings, a crawl ID, and linked immersive website IDs. The proposed `game_engines` collection stores an ObjectId, name, version, and website URL; `platforms` stores an ObjectId, name, and website URL.

The proposed `web_crawls` collection records an ObjectId, timestamp, total website count, new website count, updated website count, and error count. The proposed `crawl_errors` collection records an ObjectId, a website ID referencing either `websites` or `classic_websites`, a crawl ID, error type (such as HTTP, timeout, or parsing), error message, and timestamp.

The proposed `crawl_queue` collection records an ObjectId, website ID referencing either `websites` or `classic_websites`, website type (`immersive` or `classic`), crawl status (`pending`, `crawling`, or `crawled`), optional assigned crawler ID, and the timestamp when the website entered the queue.

The assistant said the schema supports metadata and relationship management for immersive and classic websites, tracking crawl events and errors, storing game engine and platform associations, recursive crawling, on-demand website additions, and multiple parallel crawlers without conflicts. The stated project context is indexing WebXR-supported sites.

Kadence’s love of music began around age six, when Kadence’s grandmother occasionally took Kadence to a woman’s home just outside Mandeville. The home had a grand piano that captivated Kadence; Kadence played random notes despite the adults’ disapproval and imagined turning them into a beautiful melody, like the Dolby Atmos intro becoming musical harmony. Kadence visited fewer than 20 times, roughly once every couple of months. Before those visits Kadence listened to music passively, but afterward wanted to create music.

Around seventh grade at deCarterate College in Mandeville, Kadence began rapping with friends. They made beats by knocking their hands on classroom tables and took turns freestyling. Kadence received recognition for word choice and flow, and people told Kadence they were destined to become a famous musician; Kadence believed them.

As a young musician, Kadence booked recording sessions at Outta Space Records, a studio run by Kadence’s friend Steelchest. Steelchest saw potential in Kadence, encouraged Kadence, and pushed Kadence to do their best at each session. Kadence released a first EP titled “Untitled” with Steelchest’s support. The EP received little attention, but Kadence remains proud of it.

Around tenth grade, Kadence first seriously tried music production. Kadence had attempted to make a beat years earlier, unsuccessfully. Kadence became close friends with Jamaican music producer SOS Dynamikz, and, while visiting best friends Marc and Matthew at their home, watched SOS Dynamikz make a beat. The process seemed easy, and the beautiful sound inspired Kadence to start making beats too.

Kadence says music activity has been on and off, with distractions including women, drugs, and money. Kadence estimates being able to create music that matches what they hear in their head with about 75% accuracy, which feels sufficient to keep working. Kadence regrets years spent not releasing music and says they have released fewer than 50 songs in total.
On February 18, 2023, Kadence said that 2023 would be completely different regarding their music releases, implying an intention to be more active about releasing music.

On February 18, 2023, the assistant explained that U.S. H-2A and H-2B petitions cover temporary or seasonal agricultural and non-agricultural work, respectively, and both use Form I-129. Employers must provide a temporary labor certification from the U.S. Department of Labor or Guam Department of Labor when required, and the number of workers requested cannot exceed the number approved in the certification.

The assistant explained that an H-2A or H-2B employer may request unnamed workers, or a mix of named and unnamed workers, if the same action is requested for each. Workers must be named if they are currently in the United States, are nationals of a country not on the eligible-country list, or must meet minimum job requirements specified in the temporary labor certification.

The assistant explained that employers may not collect prohibited fees, such as job-placement fees, from H-2A or H-2B beneficiaries; such fees can result in petition denial or revocation. Employers must provide evidence, to the best of their knowledge, that beneficiaries have not paid and will not pay prohibited fees. For an interrupted stay, employers must provide evidence of beneficiaries’ continuous physical presence in the United States and outside the United States during the interrupted stay.
